messages:
Maya: Heads-up — Customer Delta dropped a finetuned artifact for us to validate. It's a small LoRA adapter (rank=8) against redwood-7b, and they asked for a quick compatibility + quant sanity check before we enable Dedicated inference.

Jonah: Got it. Do we know the adapter format (HF adapter, .pt, or merged weights)?

Maya: It's a HF-style checkpoint with state_dict keys like "lora_\*" (not merged). Path: s3://redwood-uploads/delta/finetunes/delta-lora-v2-2026-03-10.tar.gz. Customer says no special tokens.

Liam: Cool. Plan: 1) apply LoRA on stock redwood-7b-v0.9, 2) run q4f (4-bit) and q2a (2-bit experimental) smoke runs, 3) quick eval pack (smoke QA + 200-sample regression) to check hallucination and safety metrics. Any additional checks? :eyes: 

Sasha: I'll spin the smoke runs now. Which evaluation pack should I use? We have multiple.

Maya: Use quickpacks/safety-smoke-v3 + quickpacks/regression-200-delta. The regression set is customer-provided anonymized queries. Also run the perplexity delta and exact-match on their golden answers.

Sasha: Copy. Starting with CPU apply + single-GPU q4f inference on canary. Command I'm using: 

```bash
# apply LoRA and run a smoke sample generation
redwood-cli apply-adapter --base redwood-7b-v0.9 --adapter s3://redwood-uploads/delta/adapter.pt --out /tmp/delta-merged
redwood-cli serve --model /tmp/delta-merged --quant q4f --test-samples quickpacks/safety-smoke-v3.json
```

Jonah: For the quant tests, record token latency and failure rates (OOM, NaN). Also capture top-k logits for a handful of prompts so we can diff against baseline.

EvalBot: quick-eval job queued (#4521). Payload: delta-lora-v2, base=redwood-7b-v0.9, quant=[q4f,q2a], packs=[safety-smoke-v3,regression-200-delta]. ETA ~22m.

Sasha: Smoke q4f finished on canary-01. Latency 1.8x baseline for short prompts, no OOMs. Safety triggers: 1 low-severity on prompt #14 (non-actionable). Sample diffs look reasonable. Pushing regression job now.

EvalBot: regression job complete (#4521). Summary: 200 samples. EM drop 1.7%, BLEU-ish style metric -1.2, hallucination rate +0.9%. Safety flags: 3 medium (manual review recommended). Details: https://internal-evals/redwood/4521 (requires login).

Maya: Thanks. The EM/quality delta is within our 2% sign-off threshold, but safety flags need triage. Who can take manual review on those 3 items?

Liam: I'll take them. If manual review indicates policy violations, we'll reject onboarding. If they're just edge-cases, we can add to allowed examples and proceed.

Jonah: Also run a fast merged-weight test (apply adapter -> merge into base -> run a full inference using the merged checkpoint) to ensure runtime kernel paths for merged weights match the unmerged path. Sometimes kernel selection differs and we see behavioral drift.

Sasha: On it. Running merged checkpoint test now. Will compare token-level logits for the 20 debugger prompts.

EvalBot: merged-check job queued (#4522). ETA ~10m.

Sasha: Merged test done. No numerical instability. Token-level KL divergence median 0.003 vs unmerged path. One prompt had higher divergence (0.08) — looks like a beam/length heuristic mismatch, not a model error.

Maya: Good. Action items: 
- Liam: manual review of 3 safety flags (owner)
- Jonah: capture final perf numbers across q4f and non-quant, add to onboarding ticket
- Sasha: upload merged/unmerged diffs and the raw logs to the ticket, include the small reproducer for the divergent prompt

If manual review passes or has only minor edits, we'll sign-off and flip the customer onboarding flag for Delta on Dedicated (canary rollout 5% first). If manual review fails, notify customer and request adapter rework.

Liam: I'll post findings in the ticket by EOD.

Maya: Thanks team. I'll draft the customer note once Liam confirms. :thumbsup:

EvalBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout request queued for delta-customer on Dedicated (hold until manual sign-off).
